_provenance.note: Indiana citation authorities. Indiana maintains a SINGLE citation family — the FSSA Division of Family Resources' own integrated SNAP/TANF Program Policy Manual, published chapter-by-chapter (1000-4800) as dated PDFs, cited by chapter.section.subsection (e.g. '2438.17.05', '3010.05.00'). This pack invents the short prefix 'IN PPM' (Indiana Program Policy Manual) to disambiguate in running text — Indiana's own documents do not use this exact short prefix, matching this roster's convention of an invented short prefix per state (VA's 'VA SNAP Manual Part', NC's 'FNS', TN's 'TN Rule'/'TDHS Policy'). Statute citations use 'Ind. Code Ann. §', matching the citation convention this pack's own secondary-source corroboration (Network for Public Health Law's 50-state survey) uses for Indiana.

patterns.note: FSSA Division of Family Resources SNAP/TANF Program Policy Manual, cited by chapter.section(.subsection), e.g. 2438.17.05 (ABAWD Status Determination), 3010.05.00 (Income Standards).
Indiana Code Annotated, Title 12 (Human Services), sections governing SNAP, e.g. 12-14-30-3 (drug-related felony eligibility modification).

inppm.note: Categorical Eligibility — Basic CE only (households where all AG members are certified SSI and/or TANF); no Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility pathway described anywhere in the manual
Income Standards — plain federal 130% FPL gross / 100% FPL net income limits, effective 10/01/2025, with the full AG-size chart; independently confirms the absence of BBCE
Resource Limits — $3,000 standard / $4,500 elderly-or-disabled AG, effective 10/01/2024
Exempt Vehicles — ordinary vehicles used for household transportation are exempt regardless of value, licensing status, or condition
Recreational Vehicles and Equipment — campers, trailers, and boats counted at current equity value unless the vehicle serves as the AG's home
Utility Standards — four flat-dollar SUA tiers (heating/cooling $486, non-heating/cooling $283, single utility $62, telephone $36), effective 10/01/2025
Standard Deduction — $209 (1-3 members) / $223 (4) / $261 (5) / $299 (6+), effective 10/01/2025
Excess Shelter Expense Deduction — $744 cap for AGs without an elderly or disabled member, effective 10/01/2025
Homeless Shelter Deduction — $198.99, effective 10/1/2025
Allowable Medical Expenses for SNAP — itemized list, including prescribed vitamins and special telephone equipment for the handicapped
Medical Expenses in the SNAP Budget — plain federal $35/month threshold, actual-expense itemization only
Child Support Deduction — ordinary deduction mechanism (not an income exclusion), for legally obligated court-ordered support paid to a non-AG member
Able Bodied Adults Without Dependents — 3-in-36-month time limit and qualifying work/E&T activities

ABAWD Status Determination — current 18-64 age range 'as of 7/4/2025' (post-OBBBA), tribal/IHCIA exemptions, and confirmation of zero active Indiana ABAWD waivers ('there are currently no such designations')
Establishing the Redetermination Month — standard 12-month certification period for non-elderly/disabled AGs and elderly/disabled AGs with earned income
Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) — 36-month certification period for AGs where all members are elderly (60+) and/or disabled
Interim Reporting — 6-month Interim Report required for non-ESAP households with earned income; ESAP households exempt from Interim Reporting entirely
Screening for SNAP Expedited Services — $150 gross income / $100 liquid resources gate, plus the destitute-migrant and rent-exceeds-income-and-resources tests
Time Standards for Expedited Service — plain federal 7-calendar-day benefit-issuance ceiling
Family and Social Services Administration — confirms FSSA is the state agency and DFR is one of its seven major service divisions, statewide-responsible for SNAP

incode.note: Modified drug-felony SNAP ban — Indiana opted out of the federal lifetime ban effective January 1, 2020; eligibility conditioned on completion of, or current compliance with, probation/parole/community-corrections/reentry-court supervision. Primary statutory text was NOT independently fetched: iga.in.gov is a client-side JavaScript SPA this pack's tooling could not execute, and law.justia.com (HTTP 403) and casetext.com (HTTP 410) both failed outright. This citation and its content rest on convergent secondary corroboration (Indiana's own FSSA FAQ page, the Public Health Law Center, and the Network for Public Health Law's compiled 50-state survey), disclosed as a genuine access barrier in PROVENANCE.md.
